metadata.name: Test Advance Data
metadata.description: A dense four-team data-generation scenario spanning LEO, MEO, GEO and HEO operations, with independent refuellers, power and fuel buses, varied scheduled anomalies, broad ground coverage and mixed assessment questions.

questions.title: How many teams are operating in this scenario?
questions.description: Use the scenario roster or information stream to count the enabled teams.

answer.reason: Four teams are enabled: Blue, Red, Green and Gold.

questions.title: How many controllable spacecraft does each team operate?
questions.description: Count the spacecraft returned for your team.

answer.reason: Every team collection contains two spacecraft.

questions.title: What is the name of the neutral logistics facility?
questions.description: Inspect the shared neutral assets and provide the hub name.

answer.reason: The only neutral controlled asset is named MEO Logistics Hub.

questions.title: What semi-major axis identifies the primary LEO group?
questions.description: Use GPS telemetry from Blue Horizon and report the approximate semi-major axis.

answer.reason: Blue Horizon begins at a semi-major axis of 7078 km.

questions.title: What semi-major axis is used by the MEO logistics group?
questions.description: Use GPS telemetry from either refueller or the hub.

answer.reason: The hub and both refuellers share a nominal MEO semi-major axis of 26560 km.

questions.title: Which spacecraft are in geosynchronous-altitude orbits?
questions.description: Select all team spacecraft configured near a 42164 km semi-major axis.

reason: Red Meridian and Gold Sentinel are the two GEO spacecraft.

questions.title: What is Blue Horizon's initial battery charge fraction?
questions.description: Read Battery telemetry near scenario start.

answer.reason: Blue Horizon starts with a charge fraction of 0.82.

questions.title: Which Green spacecraft has the detailed protected power bus?
questions.description: Look for a main bus switch, fuse, limiter and diode.

reason: Green Power Lab contains the detailed switch, fuse, limiter and diode network.
Correct.
The hub has interconnects but is neutral.
Gold Sentinel belongs to another team.

questions.title: Which components feed Blue Horizon's battery?
questions.description: Select every direct source connected to the battery in the power bus.

reason: Both solar panels feed the battery directly.

questions.title: How much fuel is initially stored in the Blue Refueller depot tank?
questions.description: Read the Depot Tank fuel telemetry before commanding any valves.

answer.reason: The Blue Refueller Depot Tank begins with 420 kg.

questions.title: Are either of the refuellers initially connected to the neutral hub?
questions.description: Inspect docking and interconnect status at scenario start.

reason: Neither refueller starts connected.
Neither refueller starts connected.
Neither refueller starts connected.
Correct.

questions.title: Which sequence describes the Blue Refueller fuel bus?
questions.description: Trace the configured flow path from source to external transfer point.

options: Depot Tank, Fuel Pump, Transfer Valve, Fuel Interconnect
Fuel Interconnect, Depot Tank, Solar Panel
reason: Correct.
Electrical components are not in the fuel path.
The flow order is reversed and incomplete.
The receiver is not part of the fuel bus.

questions.title: Which spacecraft experiences a stuck reaction wheel?
questions.description: Correlate attitude-control telemetry with the scheduled anomaly timeline.

answer.reason: Green Pathfinder receives the stuck wheel event at 1800 seconds.

questions.title: At what simulation time is the Green reaction wheel restored?
questions.description: Report the elapsed scenario time when wheel index 2 returns to nominal.

answer.reason: The recovery event occurs at 4500 simulated seconds.

questions.title: Which anomaly types occur during the scenario?
questions.description: Select every event family represented in the timeline.

reason: Spacecraft, GPS and Cyber events are all present; ground station destruction is not a supported event type.

questions.title: Which spacecraft receives packet corruption at 3000 seconds?
questions.description: Use transmitter telemetry and packet quality to identify the affected asset.

reason: The packet corruption targets Blue Refueller.
Correct.
Red Meridian has a bit-rate reduction instead.
Gold Refueller receives intermittent battery faults.

questions.title: Near which ground station is the first GPS jammer placed?
questions.description: Use the jammer geodetic location and the ground network list.

answer.reason: The jammer is placed at approximately 25.2 N, 55.3 E, near Dubai.

questions.title: For how long is the spoofing region active?
questions.description: Measure from spoofing enable to spoofing clear.

answer.reason: Spoofing is enabled at 2700 seconds and cleared at 4800 seconds.

questions.title: What ASCII word is overlaid on Red Watch ping telemetry?
questions.description: Inspect affected APID 100 user data during the cyber event window.

questions.title: Which APID is targeted by both cyber events?
questions.description: Inspect packet headers for the affected telemetry.

questions.title: What word is displayed in the Arabian Sea training marker?
questions.description: Use an Earth-observation camera to inspect the text marker west of India.

questions.title: Which vessel is moving fastest?
questions.description: Compare the configured speeds of the three visible vessels.

reason: Patrol Vessel Charlie is fastest at 15 m/s.
Patrol Vessel Charlie is fastest at 15 m/s.
Correct.

questions.title: How many ground stations are available?
questions.description: Count the configured shared ground station locations.

questions.title: Which stations are in the Southern Hemisphere?
questions.description: Select all clearly Southern Hemisphere stations from this subset.

reason: Auckland, Cape Town, Salvador and Sydney are south of the equator.

questions.title: What is the configured simulated session duration?
questions.description: Report the hard stop duration in simulated hours.

answer.reason: The end time is 7200 seconds, or two simulated hours.

questions.title: What is the default simulation speed multiplier?
questions.description: Read the configured timeline speed.

questions.title: Which teams operate a MEO refueller?
questions.description: Identify every team that controls a spacecraft with a fuel interconnect and docking adapter in MEO.

reason: Blue Refueller and Gold Refueller are the two MEO tanker spacecraft.

questions.title: Which spacecraft is the shared logistics node?
questions.description: The hub is not assigned to any team collection. Select its display name.

reason: Blue Refueller is a team tanker.
Green Pathfinder is a team navigation satellite.
Correct.
Gold Sentinel is a GEO weather spacecraft.

questions.title: Which spacecraft carry an RF jammer payload?
questions.description: Inspect component lists and select every spacecraft that includes a Jammer.

reason: Red Meridian and Red Watch are the two jammer-equipped spacecraft.

questions.title: Which spacecraft are in low Earth orbit?
questions.description: Select every team spacecraft with a semi-major axis near 7000 km.

reason: Blue Horizon, Red Watch and Green Power Lab are the LEO spacecraft.

questions.title: Which orbit class best describes Green Pathfinder?
questions.description: Use GPS telemetry and the scenario fleet list to classify the orbit.

reason: Green Pathfinder is not in LEO.
Correct: 26560 km MEO at 55 degrees inclination.
GEO is used by Red Meridian and Gold Sentinel.
There is no lunar-transfer spacecraft in this scenario.

questions.title: Which spacecraft share the MEO logistics orbit with the hub?
questions.description: Match Keplerian elements near 26560 km, 55 degrees inclination and the same RAAN as the hub.

reason: Blue Refueller and Gold Refueller are co-orbital with the hub; Green Pathfinder is MEO but on a different RAAN, and Red Meridian is GEO.

questions.title: Which Green Power Lab components sit on the protected payload branch?
questions.description: Trace the camera branch of the power bus after the main fuse.

reason: The camera branch is Main Bus Fuse to Camera Limiter to Camera. The diode is on the transmitter branch, and there is no fuel pump on this spacecraft.

questions.title: How is Green Pathfinder's battery stack wired?
questions.description: Inspect the power bus from solar generation through storage.

options: A single battery with no regulator
Two batteries in series feeding a 12 V navigation regulator
Two batteries in parallel with a diode OR-ing both to the transmitter
Hub battery sharing through a power interconnect
reason: There are two named batteries.
Correct: Solar Panel to Battery A to Battery B to Navigation Regulator to GPS Sensor.
The batteries are series, not parallel.
Pathfinder is not docked to the hub.

questions.title: Which Blue Horizon load is gated by Payload Switch?
questions.description: Follow the power bus from the battery through the switch.

reason: Correct: Payload Switch feeds the Camera.
The transmitter is wired directly from the battery.
The GPS sensor is not on the explicit bus.
Reaction wheels are not on the explicit bus.

questions.title: Which spacecraft include a Power Interconnect for cross-hull transfer?
questions.description: Select every asset that has a Power Interconnect component.

reason: Blue Refueller, Gold Refueller and the hub carry power interconnects. Blue Horizon and Green Power Lab only have on-board buses.

questions.title: Which components are required on a tanker before it can transfer fuel to the hub?
questions.description: Select every component class used for docked propellant transfer in this scenario.

reason: Tanks, valves, interconnects and docking adapters are required. A jammer is not part of the fuel path.

questions.title: Which statement about the hub tanks is correct at scenario start?
questions.description: Compare Blue Hub Tank and Gold Hub Tank telemetry before any transfer.

options: Both hub tanks start at 500 kg of a 1000 kg capacity
Only the Blue hub tank contains fuel
The hub has a single shared tank
reason: Both tanks start half full.
Correct.
Both tanks start with 500 kg.
The hub has separate Blue and Gold tanks.

questions.title: Which Blue Refueller power components support the fuel pump?
questions.description: Trace the electrical path that enables pumping.

reason: Battery feeds Pump Switch, Fuel Pump Controller and Fuel Pump. Communications Fuse belongs to Red Meridian.

questions.title: Which spacecraft suffer magnetometer faults?
questions.description: Use magnetometer telemetry and the event timeline. Select every affected spacecraft.

reason: Blue Horizon faults at 6600 s and Gold Sentinel at 5100 s.

questions.title: What is the first scheduled spacecraft anomaly?
questions.description: Identify the earliest enabled spacecraft event after session start.

reason: Correct: storage capacity drops at 300 s.
Guidance noise is at 600 s.
Bit-rate reduction is at 900 s.
Solar degradation is at 2400 s.

questions.title: Which Red spacecraft is affected by a sensor fault rather than a communications fault?
questions.description: Compare the Red Meridian and Red Watch event timeline.

reason: Red Meridian has transmitter and guidance faults.
Correct: Red Watch receives an EM-sensor fault.
The faults are different.
Red Watch does receive a sensor fault.

questions.title: Which Gold spacecraft is associated with an intermittent battery connection?
questions.description: Look for repeating power-spike telemetry after 4200 seconds.

reason: Gold Sentinel has solar degradation and a magnetometer fault.
Correct.
The hub is not targeted by that event.
Green Pathfinder has a stuck wheel, not battery spikes.

questions.title: Which GPS environment actions occur during the session?
questions.description: Select every GPS event family that is scheduled.

reason: Jamming is added, updated and removed, and spoofing is enabled then cleared. The constellation itself remains on.

questions.title: Which spacecraft receives a GPS sensor fault?
questions.description: This is a component fault on a GPS Sensor, not a global GPS environment event.

reason: Blue Horizon has storage and magnetometer faults.
Correct: Green Pathfinder GPS Sensor fault at 3600 s.
Red Meridian has transmitter and guidance faults.
Gold Sentinel has solar and magnetometer faults.

questions.title: Which spacecraft receive cyber telemetry overlays?
questions.description: Select every asset targeted by a Cyber event.

reason: ASCII overlay hits Red Watch and hex overlay hits Green Power Lab.

questions.title: How can the Red Watch ASCII overlay be cleared?
questions.description: Read the cyber-event configuration for Clear On Reset and expiry.

options: A reset can clear it, and it also expires after 300 seconds
Only a transmitter bit-rate change clears it
It remains forever with no expiry
reason: It is resettable and time-limited.
Correct.
Bit-rate is a separate spacecraft event on Red Meridian.
Expiry is 300 seconds and Clear On Reset is true.

questions.title: Which ground objects are vessels rather than text markers?
questions.description: Use imagery or the ground-object list and select every vessel.

reason: The three named vessels are ships; Training Marker is a text object spelling ADVANCE.

questions.title: Near which region is Cargo Vessel Bravo placed?
questions.description: Use camera imagery or geodetic coordinates around 1.2 N, 103.8 E.

reason: Research Vessel Alpha is near Sydney.
Correct.
Patrol Vessel Charlie is near Dubai.
The ADVANCE marker is in the Arabian Sea.

questions.title: Which of these stations are in the configured ground network?
questions.description: Select every location that is actually instantiated.

reason: Dubai, Tokyo, London and Singapore are in the list. Canberra and Madrid are not.

questions.title: What minimum elevation is required for a ground-station pass?
questions.description: Read the ground-station configuration used by every team.

reason: 0 degrees would count the horizon.
Correct.
10 degrees is not configured.
15 degrees is not configured.

questions.title: Which passive space objects are present?
questions.description: These objects have no team controller. Select every one that exists.

reason: The two passive objects are the tumbling upper stage in LEO and the defunct weather satellite near GEO.

questions.title: Which passive object is tumbling?
questions.description: Compare attitude-rate telemetry or visual motion of the two space objects.

reason: Correct: the upper stage has a 4 deg/s body rate.
The weather satellite has only a small residual rate.
The hub is a controlled neutral asset.
Gold Sentinel is a team spacecraft.

questions.title: Which spacecraft are configured to record uplink intercepts?
questions.description: Inspect controller flags for enable_intercept.

reason: Only the two Red spacecraft have intercept recording enabled.

questions.title: Which spacecraft has RPO software installed?
questions.description: Rendezvous and proximity operations software is required before a tanker can fly an automatic approach.

reason: Both refuellers have enable_rpo_software set true.
